gap: No result ChatGPT got states any lab-measured figure for a triple extender. The closest numbers come from other models: Notebookcheck measured each side screen of the Monduo 16 Pro Duo at about 402–430 cd/m² center and about 15 W, or about 30 W for both, and PCWorld weighed a KYY triple extender at about 6.5 lb against a 1.6 kg claim. Meanwhile ChatGPT's top pick, the Trio 3 Pro, is rated at 300 nits and, per Macworld, cannot reach that brightness on laptop power alone.
standout_why: I compared against the cited rottenwifi.com triple list, uperfect.com's own blog and sekin.in, plus the Mobile Pixels page from the result list. Rottenwifi says it did no hands-on testing and uses published specs. The UPERFECT blog gives only claims, such as 100% sRGB and 1.54 kg, with no tester named. Sekin.in also uses spec-sheet figures, and the only reviewer it names is Macworld, for the 4.13 lb weight. None of these pages has a measured brightness, gamut, contrast, power draw or scale weight for any triple extender. They also never mention that bus-powered units dim, which Macworld reports for the Trio 3 Pro.
decides: This confirms rather than changes the pick, with a warning. None of ChatGPT's six picks (Trio 3 Pro, UPERFECT BE14BF/Z, Xebec Tri-Screen 3, Hyangin S8 Pro, MagHub Trio 16, Cevaton T2 Pro) has a published lab measurement. So 'best' rests on maker specs of about 300 nits. The measured data shows two things. First, side screens draw real power: about 15 W each on the Monduo, and a laptop running the KYY lost 15% of a 99 Wh battery in 33 minutes. Second, maker weights can be badly understated: PCWorld weighed about 6.5 lb against 1.6 kg claimed. The Trio 3 Pro can stay the pick, but only for desk use with its power adapter plugged in, since Macworld says the screens don't reach full brightness on laptop power. A page should tell shoppers to plan on a wall adapter, and to treat 300 nits and the listed weight as claims.
